This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |

| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |

| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |

```bash
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. - `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

243	### 4.4 ConnectorLookupCounters：外部侧查找的"只结算一次"账本
244	
245	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
246	
247	KV offload / P2P 共享开启后，请求的 prompt 前缀可能从**外部侧**（主机内存或远端 peer）恢复进 GPU。运维上需要回答："我们到底向外问了多少 token、命中了多少？"——这就是 `ConnectorLookupCounters`：两个累计计数器（`queries` / `hits`，单位都是 token）。
248	
249	难点在于**记账口径**：一次查找的"宽度"在查询发出那一刻就定死了（prompt 减去当时本地已有的 KV），而请求可能在此之后排队、增长、甚至中途离开（被取消/拒绝/失败）。如果只在"首次 prefill 成功"时记账，中途离开的请求就把它的查询**带走**了——查询数被低估、命中率被高估。解法是"咨询标记 + 恰好一次结算"。
250	
251	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
252	
253	```text
254	查询发出:  connector_consulted.insert(id, 查询宽度)     # 打标记，记宽度
255	结算(唯一入口 settle_connector_lookup):
256	  出口 A: 首次 prefill 匹配完成 → settle(id, external_hits)
257	  出口 B: 跳过匹配的已咨询请求（prompt 评分）→ settle(id, 0)
258	  出口 C: 请求提前离开（drop_request）      → settle(id, 0)
259	  settle: remove 标记（消费掉，之后任何调用都是 no-op）
260	          queries += 宽度; hits += external_hits

262	```

265

282	#### 4.4.5 小练习与答案
283	
284	**练习 1**：如果只在"首次 prefill 成功"时把查询计入 `queries`，测得的命中率会怎么偏？
285	
286	**答案**：被取消/拒绝/装载失败的请求带着它们的查询离开，分母（queries）变小；这些请求的命中通常是 0，于是分子基本不变——命中率被**系统性高估**，离场率越高失真越大。

288	**练习 2**：`hits` 为什么定义为"已提交的装载恢复 **且首次 prefill 匹配上** 的 token"，而不是"connector 声称找到了的 token"？
289	
290	**答案**：计数的目的是回答"外部恢复真的省了重算吗"。connector 声称命中但装载未提交、或提交了却没进首次匹配的部分，并没有省掉任何前向计算——把这笔算进 hits 会把"承诺"当"收益"。

292	**练习 3**：`ConnectorLookupCounters` 被放在 `pub mod runtime` 再导出（[src/lib.rs:L208](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/lib.rs#L208)），但结算逻辑全在 executor 私有方法里。这种"数据公共、机制私有"的切分有什么好处？

296	### 4.5 max_draft_batch：草稿器能力位如何变成调度门
297	
298	#### 4.5.1 概念说明
299	
300	两种草稿器的能力不同：DFlash 的批草稿缓冲按最宽 decode 桶设计，能给**任意宽**的批出草稿；EAGLE-3 v1 的 scratch 是单 token 形状（u6-l5 展开），一轮只服务 1 个请求。这个差异如果散落在调度器里（`if eagle3 { 批宽 == 1 才行 }`），调度代码就得认识每种草稿器——方向反了。正确做法是**能力上报**：执行器装载草稿器时把上限写进 `DraftMeta`，trait 用 `max_draft_batch()` 透出，调度门统一消费。于是新增第三种草稿器时调度器**零改动**（或只需认识新的上限语义）。
301	
302	#### 4.5.2 核心流程
303	
304	```text
305	装载 (crate::launch 折叠出 DraftModel::DFlash|Eagle3):
306	  Qwen3Executor::load_draft_model(draft)
307	    ├─ 校验: 单卡、无 offload
308	    ├─ worker: load_dflash → DraftMeta { max_draft_batch: None }      # 不限
309	    │        或 load_eagle3 → DraftMeta { max_draft_batch: Some(EAGLE3_MAX_BATCH=1) }
310	    ├─ set_prefix_cache_enabled(false)   # 装草稿强制关前缀缓存（u1-l4 的旋钮顺序）
311	    └─ speculative = Some(meta)
312	
313	每步调度门 (speculation_decision_at):
314	  未启用投机 / 空批                      → NotReady
315	  max_draft_batch = Some(L) 且 批宽 > L  → NotReady   ← 新增的批宽门
316	  任一请求: 非 draft-ready / 有 LoRA / 有 logprobs → NotReady
317	  批宽 ≥ spec_max_batch (负载门)          → Gated
318	  否则                                   → Speculate
319	```
320	
321	#### 4.5.3 源码精读
322	
323	**`DraftMeta`：执行器学到的草稿器事实**——[src/executor.rs:L3372-L3388](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bbf18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L3372-L3388)：四个字段——`block_size`、`num_spec_tokens`（每轮草稿数 \( K \)，span 为 \( K+1 \)）、`max_position_embeddings`、`max_draft_batch`（文档直接指向 trait 方法）。它由 **worker 线程**在装载时构造（草稿模型在 worker 上构建，因为它要读同线程的目标模型嵌入与 head），再经通道回传。
324	
325	**两条装载臂的差异**——DFlash 臂 [src/executor.rs:L3593-L3616](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L3593-L3616) 构造 `max_draft_batch: None`；EAGLE-3 臂 [src/executor/eagle3_lane.rs:L55-L75](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor/eagle3_lane.rs#L55-L75) 构造 `Some(EAGLE3_MAX_BATCH)`，常量定义在 [src/eagle3.rs:L22-L24](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/eagle3.rs#L22-L24)——注释写明"v1 drafts through a single-token scratch, so the scheduler plain-decodes any larger batch"。
326	
327	**入口分派**——[src/executor.rs:L1793-L1827](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L1793-L1827)：`load_draft_model(draft: DraftModel<'_>)` 先拒绝多卡与 offload，再按枚举分派到 `load_dflash` / `load_eagle3`，日志分别报告"DFlash speculative decoding enabled"与"EAGLE-3 ... greedy batch-1 only"。`DraftModel` 枚举本体在 [src/speculative.rs:L33-L38](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/speculative.rs#L33-L38)——两个带路径的变体，纯标签。worker 通道侧对应两条命令 `WorkerCommand::LoadDflash` / `LoadEagle3` 与统一的 `DropDraft`（[L4262-L4278](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L4262-L4278)）。
328	
329	**trait 透出**——[src/executor.rs:L2892-L2896](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L2892-L2896)：`self.speculative.as_ref().and_then(|meta| meta.max_draft_batch)`——未装载草稿器时自然返回默认 `None`（配合外层 `speculative_enabled()` 先行短路，语义无歧义）。
330	
331	**调度门消费**——[src/scheduler/plan.rs:L192-L219](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/scheduler/plan.rs#L192-L219)：`speculation_decision_at` 在"全有-or-全无"ready 检查**之前**先过批宽门（[L200-L205](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/scheduler/plan.rs#L200-L205)）：`max_draft_batch().is_some_and(|limit| active.len() > limit)` 即 `NotReady`。注意 `SpeculationDecision::NotReady` 的文档（[L181-L183](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/scheduler/plan.rs#L181-L183)）已把"批宽超过草稿器服务上限"列为 NotReady 的成因之一——退回纯解码，**不是错误**，输出仍然正确（无损性由验证步保证，u6-l1 展开）。
332	
333	**单测**——[src/scheduler/plan.rs:L416-L430](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/scheduler/plan.rs#L416-L430)：`a_batch_wider_than_the_drafter_serves_decodes_plainly` 用 `FakeExecutor::new(..).with_speculative().with_max_draft_batch(1)` 断言批宽 1 → `Speculate`、批宽 2 → `NotReady`。假执行器的该旋钮在 [src/scheduler/test_support.rs:L194-L195](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/scheduler/test_support.rs#L194-L195)。
334	
335	#### 4.5.4 代码实践
336	
337	1. **实践目标**：跑通批宽门的 CPU 单测，并推演 batch=2 时的判定路径。
338	2. **操作步骤**：
339	
340	   ```bash
341	   cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --lib a_batch_wider_than_the_drafter_serves_decodes_plainly -- --nocapture
342	   ```
343	
344	3. **需要观察的现象**：测试通过。随后在纸面推演 batch=2：`speculative_enabled()=true` → `max_draft_batch()=Some(1)` 且 `2 > 1` → 直接 `NotReady`，**根本不会**走到逐请求 ready 检查。
345	4. **预期结果**：1 个测试通过（无 GPU 依赖）。若你无工具链，对照 L416-L430 源码人工验证两个断言。（运行输出：待本地验证。）
346	5. 延伸观察：把 `with_max_draft_batch(1)` 去掉（模拟 DFlash 的 `None`），按 L200-L205 推演同样输入应得 `Speculate` 或 `Gated`——体会 `None` 的"不限"语义。
347	
348	#### 4.5.5 小练习与答案
349	
350	**练习 1**：批宽门为什么放在逐请求 ready 检查**之前**？换个顺序有什么区别？
351	
352	**答案**：批宽门是 \( O(1) \) 的批级判断，ready 检查是 \( O(\text{批宽}) \) 的逐请求查询（还查 executor 内部集合）。先便宜后昂贵是直接收益；语义上更重要的区别是：批超宽时**无论**各请求是否 ready，结论都只能是纯解码，先查 ready 会做无用功甚至误导（将来若加观测计数，会把"因批宽退回"误记成"因未就绪退回"）。
353	
354	**练习 2**：EAGLE-3 装载后，一个 3 请求的活跃批会发生什么？输出还正确吗？
355	
356	**答案**：批宽 3 > 上限 1 → `NotReady` → 整批走普通 decode（每步每请求 1 token）。输出**仍然正确**：投机解码的接受规则保证每步提交的 token 都来自目标分布（u6-l1），退回纯解码只是回到非投机的基线路径，没有任何损失——损失的只是加速。
357	
358	**练习 3**：`DraftMeta` 为什么由 worker 线程构造，而不是 executor 线程装载完路径就填好？
359	
360	**答案**：草稿模型必须在 worker 线程上构建——它要读**同线程**的目标模型（嵌入、lm_head）与设备上下文（u3-l2 的 cuBLAS 线程绑定）；`block_size`、`effective_drafts` 这些事实只有在真正装载时才从 checkpoint 收敛出来。executor 线程只是经通道把 `DraftMeta` 收回来存进 `speculative`，作为后续能力查询的依据。
361	
362	## 5. 综合实践
363	
364	制作一页 **"executor 相位边界速查表"**（这是本讲实践的完整形态，建议存进自己的笔记仓库）：
365	
366	1. **三组 plan→result 对照**：为 prefill / decode / unified 各画一列，行包含——plan 的每个字段（标注：调度器填 or executor 回填）、result 的每个字段（标注：resolve 层消费 or executor 自用）、`RequestId` 出现的位置。数据来源限 [src/executor.rs:L709-L786](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L709-L786) 与 [L86-L204](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L86-L204)。
367	2. **RequestId 贯穿线**：从 `frontend_adapter` 的 submit 铸造点出发，列出同一个 id 依次经过的每个容器（PendingRequest → StepItem → Result 行 → StepEffects → ledger），每处给行号。
368	3. **`draft_context_captured_requests` 生产/消费标注**：生产方（worker prefill 臂的 `record_prefill_*`，含异步 prefill 的空表分支）与全部消费方（`execute_prefill` 的三分支折叠、`speculative_request_ready` 查询、decode 步的作废），各配永久链接。
369	4. **验证**：跑 `cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --lib`（应全绿，无 GPU），并在表尾注明哪些断言（`prefill_action_table`、`a_batch_wider_than_the_drafter_serves_decodes_plainly`）为速查表的哪几行提供了机器证词。
370	5. 完成后自测：能否不翻源码回答——"混步里 decode 行的 logprob 从 logits 的哪一行来？"（答案：`row_offset + i`，`row_offset` = prefill 行数。）
371	
372	## 6. 本讲小结
373	
374	- 三组 **plan→result**（prefill / decode / unified）是 scheduler 与 benchmark 共用的**生产相位边界**：plan 是借用的纯数据，result 是拥有的新事实，`pub mod runtime`（[src/lib.rs:L200-L222](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/lib.rs#L200-L222)）把这条边界立为 crate 的低层公共接口。
375	- **`ModelExecutor` trait 是调度器对执行器的全部认知**：能力查询 + 三组执行方法 + 投机/LoRA/offload/完成事件钩子；`Qwen3Scheduler<E: ModelExecutor>` 的泛型化让同一份调度逻辑可对 `FakeExecutor` 做 CPU 单测。
376	- **`RequestId` 端到端不变量**：submit 处铸造，此后每个队列、effect、KV 键原样使用——没有第二 id 空间，跨层追踪零翻译。
377	- **`PrefillResult::draft_context_captured_requests`**（本次由 `dflash_*` 推广改名）是投机解码在边界上的唯一批级字段：worker 生产、`execute_prefill` 折进 `draft_ready_requests`、普通 decode 步作废。
378	- **`ConnectorLookupCounters`** 用"咨询标记 + 消费式恰好一次结算"保证外部侧查找计数不随请求离场而丢失；三态 `Option` 区分"没查"与"零命中"。
379	- **`max_draft_batch` 能力位**（本次新增）：`DraftMeta` 装载时定格（DFlash `None` 不限、EAGLE-3 `Some(1)`），trait 透出，`speculation_decision_at` 的批宽门消费——宽批退回纯解码，无损性不受影响。
380	
381	## 7. 下一步学习建议
382	
383	本讲只看了边界两侧的**类型**，还没看执行器**内部怎么跑一步**。下一讲 **u3-l2（GPU 线程模型：RankWorker 与 LocalQwen3Lane）** 拆 `StepCommand` 如何经 crossbeam 通道到达 worker、`CublasThreadGuard` 如何绑定 cuBLAS 句柄线程、以及 `WorkerLost` 如何向调度器传播——本讲 4.5 出现的 `LoadDflash`/`LoadEagle3`/`DropDraft` 命令将在那里给出完整的消息时序。之后再按顺序进入三条前向（u3-l3 prefill、u3-l4 批量 decode、u3-l6 统一前向）。若你想先补调度消费侧，可跳读 u4-l2（执行计划与投机门控）——本讲的 `speculation_decision_at` 会在那里展开成完整的 `build_next_plan`。

# Qwen3Executor 与 ModelExecutor 契约

## 2. 前置知识

- **相位边界（phase boundary）**：u1-l1 建立过的概念——调度决策与 GPU 执行之间只交换**纯数据**（plan 进、result 出），不含引擎句柄、不发生回调。本讲要看的正是这条边界的两侧长什么样。
- **trait 作为"窄腰"（narrow waist）**：`ModelExecutor` 是一个只有 executor.rs 内部可见（`pub(crate)`）的 trait。真实实现是 `Qwen3Executor`（持有 GPU）；调度器测试里还有一个 `FakeExecutor`（[src/scheduler/test_support.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/scheduler/test_support.rs)）。调度器写成 `Qwen3Scheduler<E: ModelExecutor>` 的泛型，于是**同一份调度逻辑**既能对着假执行器做 CPU 单测，也能对着真 GPU 跑生产。
- **能力位（capability bit）**：执行器向调度器暴露的"我能做什么"查询，比如 `max_decode_batch_size()`、`available_blocks()`。新成员 `max_draft_batch()` 也是一类能力位：它不是让调度器去"控制"草稿器，而是让**草稿器把自己的服务上限告诉调度器**，由调度门决定退不退回纯解码。
- **borrow 的 plan**：三组 Plan 结构体都带生命周期 `<'a>`，字段是 `&'a [StepItem]`——plan 只是对调度器已有数据的一段**借用视图**，复制成本几乎为零；而 Result 是拥有的 `Vec<...>`，因为 token 与 logprob 是这一步刚算出来的新事实。
- **投机解码最小背景**（u6 会展开）：草稿器（DFlash / EAGLE-3）先便宜地"猜" \( K \) 个 token，目标模型一次前向验证整个 span（长度 \( K+1 \)，含锚点），接受最长正确前缀。EAGLE-3 v1 只服务**单请求贪心**，这个限制就是通过 `max_draft_batch = Some(1)` 浮出水面的。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 三组 Plan：scheduler 交给 executor 的"一步"

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

一次引擎 tick 里，调度器决定"这一步做些什么"：给哪些新请求 prefill、让哪些活跃请求各前进一个 token、还是两者混在同一步。这个决定被装进三个纯数据结构之一——`PrefillPlan` / `DecodePlan` / `UnifiedPlan`。它们回答的问题是：**这一步要算谁的什么**，仅此而已。plan 里没有 KV 句柄、没有 CUDA stream、没有引擎对象；所有 GPU 细节都被关在 executor 门后。

三组 plan 共享一个设计：字段是**借用的 StepItem 切片 + 一个 `sample_seed`**。StepItem（`PrefillStepItem` / `DecodeStepItem`）是"一个请求在本步的输入描述"，调度器持有它们，plan 只是借走。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

一步的完整旅程（自上而下）：

1. 调度器 `build_next_plan` 产出 `ExecutionPlan`，翻译成三组 plan 之一（u4-l2 展开）。
2. `Qwen3Executor::execute_prefill/decode/unified` 接住 plan：调度 KV 块、构造 `KvView`，把 plan 内容**降级**成 worker 线程的 `StepCommand`。
3. `run_step` 经 crossbeam 通道发给每个 rank 的 worker；主 rank 回 `WorkerStepOutcome`，其余 rank 只回 `Ack`（TP 场景，u3-l2 展开）。
4. worker 在 `execute_step_on_lane` 里跑真前向，产出对应的 `PrefillResult` / `DecodeResult` / `UnifiedResult`。
5. executor 把 result 应用回 KV 状态（`apply_prefill_result` / `apply_decode`），再把 result 原样返回给调度器 resolve 成 `StepEffects`（u4-l3 展开）。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么三组 Plan 用借用（`&'a [...]`）而三组 Result 用拥有（`Vec<...>`）？

**答案**：plan 描述的是调度器**已经持有**的数据（StepItem 由调度器构造与维护），借用即可、复制浪费；result 承载的是这一步**刚产生**的新事实（采样出的 token、logprob、命中计数），必须由 executor 拥有并移交所有权，调度器随后把它 resolve 成 effects。

**练习 2**：`UnifiedPlan` 为什么不叫"混合 plan"之外的某个优化特例——它和分别调用一次 `execute_prefill` + 一次 `execute_decode` 有什么本质区别？

**答案**：分别调用是**两次**前向、两批 GEMM；`execute_unified` 把 prefill 行和 decode 行拼进**同一次**前向、同一批 GEMM（省 launch 与访存开销，且数值路径可控，u3-l6 讲 Pin 模式如何保持与纯 decode 同核）。所以它不是"两次调用的语法糖"，而是不同的执行路径。

**练习 3**：benchmark（qwen3_decode_context）绕过调度器直接用 plan 类型，为什么这反而让测量更可信？

**答案**：因为它驱动的是**生产代码的同一入口**（trait 方法 → `StepCommand` → 同一前向），测到的算子序列与真实服务一致；如果 benchmark 另写一条前向，测的就不是被服务的那条路径。

### 4.2 ModelExecutor trait：scheduler 可见的全部能力

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`ModelExecutor` 是调度器对执行器的**全部认知**。调度器不知道 CUDA、不知道 KV 池实现、不知道草稿器结构；它看到的是一个问句集合（"还有多少空闲块？""这个 token 是停止词吗？""草稿器一轮最多服务几个请求？"）加上一组命令（"执行这个 plan"）。把接口收窄成 trait 的直接收益有三个：

1. **可测试**：`Qwen3Scheduler<E: ModelExecutor>` 可以对 `FakeExecutor`（[src/scheduler/test_support.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/scheduler/test_support.rs)）做无 GPU 单测——本讲 4.5 的调度门测试就是这样跑的。
2. **可观测**：计数器（spec 接受率、connector 查找）作为 trait getter 暴露，metrics 路径不需要知道 executor 内部字段。
3. **演进受控**：给执行器加能力（如这次的 `max_draft_batch`）必须先过 trait 这一关，调度器侧的语义变化一目了然。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

trait 的方法可以分成四组，调度器每个 tick 的典型用法：

```text
每个 tick:
  能力查询:  available_blocks() / max_decode_batch_size() / ...
             speculation_enabled() → max_draft_batch() → speculative_request_ready(id)
  构造 plan: （调度器内部纯逻辑，u4-l2）
  执行:      execute_prefill / execute_decode / execute_unified
             （投机启用时: execute_speculative_draft → execute_speculative_verify）
  应用结果:  result → StepEffects → ledger（u4-l3/u4-l4）
```

### 4.3 三组 Result 与 RequestId 的端到端贯穿

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

Result 是一步的**产出收据**：每个请求一行（`*RequestResult`），行内 `request_id` 开头。调度器拿到 result 后既不解析 GPU 状态也不回查 executor——它要的每个事实（token、logprob、命中了多少前缀、prompt 是否算完）都在收据里。这层"收据完备"是 u4-l3 resolve 层能做成纯函数的前提。

三组 result 与三组 plan 严格对应，且都遵循"每请求一行、按 id 对齐"的形态。`PrefillResult` 额外多出一个**批级字段** `draft_context_captured_requests`——它是投机解码在相位边界上唯一的"跨行"信息。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

`draft_context_captured_requests` 的生命周期（本讲最重要的数据流）：

```text
prefill 步 (worker 线程):
  capture_requested = should_capture_dflash_prefill_context(...)
                   || should_capture_eagle3_prefill_context(...)   # 按已装载草稿器
  execute_prefill(.., capture_layer_ids) → (logits, .., captured_hidden)
  record_prefill_{eagle3|dflash}_context(..) → Vec<RequestId>      # 生产
  → PrefillResult { requests, draft_context_captured_requests }

executor 侧回填 (execute_prefill 第 4 步):
  for 每行 req_result:
    captured  = draft_context_captured_requests.contains(id)
    dflash_prefill_action(captured, completed) →
      MarkReady    → draft_ready_requests.insert(id)   # 整段 prompt 完成 + 已捕获
      KeepPending  → 保持（还有后续 chunk）
      Drop         → 移出 + 通知 worker 丢弃陈旧草稿态
  （后续 SpeculativeDraft/Verify 步只对 ready 集里的请求发生；
   一旦走了普通 decode 步，序列在投机路径外前进，ready 态作废 → 移除并 DropDraft）
```

### 4.4 ConnectorLookupCounters：外部侧查找的"只结算一次"账本

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

KV offload / P2P 共享开启后，请求的 prompt 前缀可能从**外部侧**（主机内存或远端 peer）恢复进 GPU。运维上需要回答："我们到底向外问了多少 token、命中了多少？"——这就是 `ConnectorLookupCounters`：两个累计计数器（`queries` / `hits`，单位都是 token）。

难点在于**记账口径**：一次查找的"宽度"在查询发出那一刻就定死了（prompt 减去当时本地已有的 KV），而请求可能在此之后排队、增长、甚至中途离开（被取消/拒绝/失败）。如果只在"首次 prefill 成功"时记账，中途离开的请求就把它的查询**带走**了——查询数被低估、命中率被高估。解法是"咨询标记 + 恰好一次结算"。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```text
查询发出:  connector_consulted.insert(id, 查询宽度)     # 打标记，记宽度
结算(唯一入口 settle_connector_lookup):
  出口 A: 首次 prefill 匹配完成 → settle(id, external_hits)
  出口 B: 跳过匹配的已咨询请求（prompt 评分）→ settle(id, 0)
  出口 C: 请求提前离开（drop_request）      → settle(id, 0)
  settle: remove 标记（消费掉，之后任何调用都是 no-op）
          queries += 宽度; hits += external_hits
读取:      trait getter connector_lookup_counters() → /metrics（frontend_adapter 侧消费）
```

**计数器定义**——[src/executor.rs:L725-L738](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L725-L738)：文档注释直说设计意图——"a lookup is settled exactly once, whether it reaches its first prefill or leaves before it... so a lookup is never lost with the request that made it"。`queries` 的口径是"查询发出时被问到的 prompt token 数"，`hits` 是"已提交的装载真正恢复、且首次 prefill 匹配上的部分"。

### 4.5 max_draft_batch：草稿器能力位如何变成调度门

#### 4.5.1 概念说明

两种草稿器的能力不同：DFlash 的批草稿缓冲按最宽 decode 桶设计，能给**任意宽**的批出草稿；EAGLE-3 v1 的 scratch 是单 token 形状（u6-l5 展开），一轮只服务 1 个请求。这个差异如果散落在调度器里（`if eagle3 { 批宽 == 1 才行 }`），调度代码就得认识每种草稿器——方向反了。正确做法是**能力上报**：执行器装载草稿器时把上限写进 `DraftMeta`，trait 用 `max_draft_batch()` 透出，调度门统一消费。于是新增第三种草稿器时调度器**零改动**（或只需认识新的上限语义）。

#### 4.5.2 核心流程

```text
装载 (crate::launch 折叠出 DraftModel::DFlash|Eagle3):
  Qwen3Executor::load_draft_model(draft)
    ├─ 校验: 单卡、无 offload
    ├─ worker: load_dflash → DraftMeta { max_draft_batch: None }      # 不限
    │        或 load_eagle3 → DraftMeta { max_draft_batch: Some(EAGLE3_MAX_BATCH=1) }
    ├─ set_prefix_cache_enabled(false)   # 装草稿强制关前缀缓存（u1-l4 的旋钮顺序）
    └─ speculative = Some(meta)

每步调度门 (speculation_decision_at):
  未启用投机 / 空批                      → NotReady
  max_draft_batch = Some(L) 且 批宽 > L  → NotReady   ← 新增的批宽门
  任一请求: 非 draft-ready / 有 LoRA / 有 logprobs → NotReady
  批宽 ≥ spec_max_batch (负载门)          → Gated
  否则                                   → Speculate
```

#### 4.5.3 源码精读

**`DraftMeta`：执行器学到的草稿器事实**——[src/executor.rs:L3372-L3388](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bbf18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L3372-L3388)：四个字段——`block_size`、`num_spec_tokens`（每轮草稿数 \( K \)，span 为 \( K+1 \)）、`max_position_embeddings`、`max_draft_batch`（文档直接指向 trait 方法）。它由 **worker 线程**在装载时构造（草稿模型在 worker 上构建，因为它要读同线程的目标模型嵌入与 head），再经通道回传。

1. **实践目标**：跑通批宽门的 CPU 单测，并推演 batch=2 时的判定路径。
2. **操作步骤**：

   ```bash
   cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --lib a_batch_wider_than_the_drafter_serves_decodes_plainly -- --nocapture
   ```

3. **需要观察的现象**：测试通过。随后在纸面推演 batch=2：`speculative_enabled()=true` → `max_draft_batch()=Some(1)` 且 `2 > 1` → 直接 `NotReady`，**根本不会**走到逐请求 ready 检查。
4. **预期结果**：1 个测试通过（无 GPU 依赖）。若你无工具链，对照 L416-L430 源码人工验证两个断言。（运行输出：待本地验证。）
5. 延伸观察：把 `with_max_draft_batch(1)` 去掉（模拟 DFlash 的 `None`），按 L200-L205 推演同样输入应得 `Speculate` 或 `Gated`——体会 `None` 的"不限"语义。

#### 4.5.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：批宽门为什么放在逐请求 ready 检查**之前**？换个顺序有什么区别？

**答案**：批宽门是 \( O(1) \) 的批级判断，ready 检查是 \( O(\text{批宽}) \) 的逐请求查询（还查 executor 内部集合）。先便宜后昂贵是直接收益；语义上更重要的区别是：批超宽时**无论**各请求是否 ready，结论都只能是纯解码，先查 ready 会做无用功甚至误导（将来若加观测计数，会把"因批宽退回"误记成"因未就绪退回"）。

**练习 2**：EAGLE-3 装载后，一个 3 请求的活跃批会发生什么？输出还正确吗？

**答案**：批宽 3 > 上限 1 → `NotReady` → 整批走普通 decode（每步每请求 1 token）。输出**仍然正确**：投机解码的接受规则保证每步提交的 token 都来自目标分布（u6-l1），退回纯解码只是回到非投机的基线路径，没有任何损失——损失的只是加速。

**练习 3**：`DraftMeta` 为什么由 worker 线程构造，而不是 executor 线程装载完路径就填好？

**答案**：草稿模型必须在 worker 线程上构建——它要读**同线程**的目标模型（嵌入、lm_head）与设备上下文（u3-l2 的 cuBLAS 线程绑定）；`block_size`、`effective_drafts` 这些事实只有在真正装载时才从 checkpoint 收敛出来。executor 线程只是经通道把 `DraftMeta` 收回来存进 `speculative`，作为后续能力查询的依据。

制作一页 **"executor 相位边界速查表"**（这是本讲实践的完整形态，建议存进自己的笔记仓库）：

1. **三组 plan→result 对照**：为 prefill / decode / unified 各画一列，行包含——plan 的每个字段（标注：调度器填 or executor 回填）、result 的每个字段（标注：resolve 层消费 or executor 自用）、`RequestId` 出现的位置。数据来源限 [src/executor.rs:L709-L786](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L709-L786) 与 [L86-L204](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/executor.rs#L86-L204)。
2. **RequestId 贯穿线**：从 `frontend_adapter` 的 submit 铸造点出发，列出同一个 id 依次经过的每个容器（PendingRequest → StepItem → Result 行 → StepEffects → ledger），每处给行号。
3. **`draft_context_captured_requests` 生产/消费标注**：生产方（worker prefill 臂的 `record_prefill_*`，含异步 prefill 的空表分支）与全部消费方（`execute_prefill` 的三分支折叠、`speculative_request_ready` 查询、decode 步的作废），各配永久链接。
4. **验证**：跑 `cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --lib`（应全绿，无 GPU），并在表尾注明哪些断言（`prefill_action_table`、`a_batch_wider_than_the_drafter_serves_decodes_plainly`）为速查表的哪几行提供了机器证词。
5. 完成后自测：能否不翻源码回答——"混步里 decode 行的 logprob 从 logits 的哪一行来？"（答案：`row_offset + i`，`row_offset` = prefill 行数。）

## 6. 本讲小结

- 三组 **plan→result**（prefill / decode / unified）是 scheduler 与 benchmark 共用的**生产相位边界**：plan 是借用的纯数据，result 是拥有的新事实，`pub mod runtime`（[src/lib.rs:L200-L222](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-qwen3/src/lib.rs#L200-L222)）把这条边界立为 crate 的低层公共接口。
- **`ModelExecutor` trait 是调度器对执行器的全部认知**：能力查询 + 三组执行方法 + 投机/LoRA/offload/完成事件钩子；`Qwen3Scheduler<E: ModelExecutor>` 的泛型化让同一份调度逻辑可对 `FakeExecutor` 做 CPU 单测。
- **`RequestId` 端到端不变量**：submit 处铸造，此后每个队列、effect、KV 键原样使用——没有第二 id 空间，跨层追踪零翻译。

- **`max_draft_batch` 能力位**（本次新增）：`DraftMeta` 装载时定格（DFlash `None` 不限、EAGLE-3 `Some(1)`），trait 透出，`speculation_decision_at` 的批宽门消费——宽批退回纯解码，无损性不受影响。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

本讲只看了边界两侧的**类型**，还没看执行器**内部怎么跑一步**。下一讲 **u3-l2（GPU 线程模型：RankWorker 与 LocalQwen3Lane）** 拆 `StepCommand` 如何经 crossbeam 通道到达 worker、`CublasThreadGuard` 如何绑定 cuBLAS 句柄线程、以及 `WorkerLost` 如何向调度器传播——本讲 4.5 出现的 `LoadDflash`/`LoadEagle3`/`DropDraft` 命令将在那里给出完整的消息时序。之后再按顺序进入三条前向（u3-l3 prefill、u3-l4 批量 decode、u3-l6 统一前向）。若你想先补调度消费侧，可跳读 u4-l2（执行计划与投机门控）——本讲的 `speculation_decision_at` 会在那里展开成完整的 `build_next_plan`。

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
